text.p: A week-long standoff between police and renegade Texas separatists ended on Saturday when four of the once-defiant rebels surrendered and two others fled on foot, according to CNN.
The report said that Republic of Texas leader Richard McClaren was among those who had given himself up to police.

Michelle O'Rourke, wife of attorney Terence O'Rourke, told Reuters that her husband had reported from inside the police command center ringing the rebels' mountain compound that four of the rebels surrendered, but the other two were still in talks with police. Police had yet to confirm any of the reports.

"They're coming out," she said. "There were four of them out there. Rick is being reunited with his wife." O'Rourke has represented McLaren and wife Evelyn in negotiations to end the siege which started on Sunday.
Evelyn McLaren left the compound earlier on Saturday after pleas from her two daughters to give up. Police said she was being held for questioning, but would likely not face charges.

The siege began on Sunday when members of the Republic, who say Texas is an independent nation, took two hostages in retaliation for the arrest of their security chief. They face felony charges arising from the kidnapping.
